I’ve been trying to isolate why the end‑to‑end test `test_full_pipeline_end_to_end` hangs. The unit tests all pass, but when I run the e2e suite it times out. I attempted to run the whole test file with a 30 s timeout, but it still timed out (exit code 143). Then I added a faulthandler dump that triggers after 20 s, hoping to capture a stack trace of the hanging thread. The first faulthandler run gave me a truncated traceback ending at the generic pytest runner frames:

```
File ".../tests/e2e/test_train_entry.py", line 71 in test_full_pipeline_end_to_end
...
File ".../_pytest/python.py", line 1720 in runtest
```

That didn’t show the deeper call stack inside my own code. I tried to narrow it down by grepping for “runtest$” and printing a few lines before, but again the output stopped at the pytest internals, without revealing the actual worker thread’s stack.

What I need now is the full stack trace from the thread that faulthandler dumps, not just the pytest wrapper frames. The faulthandler output includes a header like “Thread 0x... (most recent call first):” followed by the stack of that thread, and later the test file’s name appears again when the traceback finishes. If I can extract everything between the start of the thread dump (“Thread 0x…”) and the point where the test file name appears (“test_train_entry”), I’ll get the complete call chain that led to the hang.

To do this, I’ll run the same Python one‑liner with faulthandler, but pipe the output through `sed`. The `sed -n '/Thread 0x/,/test_train_entry/p'` command will print only the lines from the beginning of the thread dump up to the line containing “test_train_entry”. I’ll then cap the output with `head -40` to avoid overwhelming the console while still capturing enough context. I’ll keep the same 30 s timeout (plus a small buffer for the command itself) and the same `-c` inline script, because I want the dump to fire after 20 s and then let pytest exit.

Thus the next step is to execute this refined command and examine the full thread stack to pinpoint where the pipeline is getting stuck.
